newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana looking to buy tanks from Austria.
newsitem.headline: Botswana looking to buy tanks from Austria.

text.p: Botswana is negotiating to buy tanks from Austria's Steyr-Daimler-Puch AG, Austria's ambassador said on Thursday.
Press reports last month quoted European industry sources as saying the mooted order was for 32 new SK 105 light tanks built by the Austrian firm, which has applied for an export licence.
"There are negotiations going on between the Botswana Defence Force and Steyr-Daimler-Puch in Vienna," Ambassador Franz Palla, who is resident in South Africa, told Reuters.
He declined to give further information.
In July last year, the German government refused to approve an order placed by the Botswana Defence Force (BDF) with the Dutch government for 50 German-made Leopard I tanks.

The sale was blocked under a North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) ruling that the manufacturer of arms has the right to veto their sale to any country out of NATO. Austria is not a member of NATO.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said at the time that Germany would not support arms sales to any Southern African Development Community (SADC) country because of tensions in the region.
In June 1995, the BDF signed a deal to buy 13 F5 fighter-bombers from Canada. Some of these aircraft have been delivered.

Botswana, a country the size of France with 1.5 million inhabitants, is the only African state which did not inherit an army at independence, and started building a defence force from scratch in 1974.
Botswana is considered a model democracy by African standards and internal conflict is almost unknown. It borders South Africa, Namibia, Angola, Zimbabwe and Zambia.
